goals: Mechanistic/quantification: estimate spatial distribution and basin-representative magnitude of vertical deep-drainage (potential recharge) across Naches soil x forcing heterogeneity
Validation: anchor the slow-state initial condition by comparing simulated water-table depth to USGS wells and the Fan 2013 prior (recharge itself is unvalidatable in-domain)
key_processes: deep drainage QDRAI / aquifer recharge QCHARGE

model_choice.rationale: ELM single-column produces per-column vertical deep-drainage/recharge fluxes and simulates WTD; stratified columns span the basin's soil and forcing heterogeneity. PFLOTRAN not invoked because no coupler exists and the ask is for ELM's recharge flux, not a solved regional aquifer.
model_choice.coupling_note: A truly laterally-closed steady-state regional water table would require ELM->PFLOTRAN groundwater coupling; not done here, but its absence is the core feasibility caveat (see requires_capabilities).

answerable: Vertical potential recharge (QDRAI/QCHARGE) magnitude and its control by soil texture
Elevation/forcing control on recharge via NLDAS-2 elevation-varying precip and snowmelt (12 km resolution)
WTD state validation against USGS wells and Fan 2013 prior

not_answerable.aspect: 'True steady-state' regional recharge reaching a laterally-equilibrated deep water table
not_answerable.why: ELM is single-column 1-D with no lateral/regional groundwater transport; per-column QDRAI is vertical potential recharge, not a laterally-closed steady-state regional flux
brief lists recharge measurements as missing in-domain
not_answerable.needs: recharge observation dataset (e.g. baseflow-separation or chloride-mass-balance estimates)

not_answerable.aspect: Sub-12 km orographic snow/precip and ridgetop SWE
not_answerable.why: NLDAS-2 12 km cells average over terrain; no within-cell lapse rate

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified (elevation-as-forcing-proxy x soil texture) + observation-pinned validation
sampling_strategy.n_justification: 3 forcing/elevation bands x 3 dominant SSURGO texture classes = 9 cells that span the two named drivers, plus 2 replicate columns in the rain-snow transition band where snowmelt-timing controls on recharge are most sensitive. This is the smallest set that resolves soil x forcing interaction without a blind grid.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Concentrate in the rain-snow transition and on coarse-textured valley/alluvial soils where deep drainage is largest and WTD is shallowest (strongest recharge signal and best-populated by USGS wells). Sparser sampling of fine-textured montane soils where recharge is drainage-limited.
sampling_strategy.replication: 2 extra columns in the transition band to capture soil variability where the recharge gradient is steepest.

sampling_plan.reason: Rain-dominated coarse alluvium: expected recharge maximum and shallowest WTD; anchors high end of recharge range.
Common valley-floor loam; typical lowland recharge under rain-dominated forcing.
Fine-textured valley soil: drainage-limited recharge end-member at low elevation.
Snowmelt-pulse infiltration into coarse soil where recharge sensitivity is highest; replicated.
Dominant transition-band soil; central estimate of snowmelt-driven recharge; replicated.
Tests whether fine texture suppresses recharge despite ample snowmelt.
High-elevation coarse soil under snow-dominated forcing (NLDAS underestimates ridge SWE).
Typical montane soil; upper-basin recharge under snow-dominated forcing.

validation_design.comparison: co-located — place validation columns at well locations and compare simulated equilibrated ZWT to measured WTD
validation_design.n_validation_points: unknown — depends on USGS well density in HUC 17030002

validation_design.comparison: co-located — Fan 2013 also supplies the warm-start IC; residual ELM 1-D vs Fan lateral-equilibrium drift is itself a reported result
no validation possible — report as model estimate only; optionally cross-check basin total against literature baseflow indices (flagged as indirect)

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: NLDAS-2 forcing (elevation-varying), native SSURGO soil, WTD-informed warm start + multi-year spin-up

requires_capabilities.why: recharge and WTD are slow states; cold start reads recharge ~0 and default 8.8 m water table
requires_capabilities.blocks: any meaningful recharge or WTD estimate

requires_capabilities.why: 'true steady-state' recharge to a regional deep water table requires lateral transport ELM lacks
requires_capabilities.blocks: answering the question as literally posed (regional steady-state recharge)

requires_capabilities.capability: recharge observation dataset (baseflow separation / chloride mass balance)

requires_capabilities.why: target variable must be written out

requires_capabilities.capability: DEM + SSURGO raster sampling and HUC boundary resolver
requires_capabilities.why: expander needs to place stratified columns by elevation band and soil class within HUC 17030002
12 km NLDAS misses sub-cell orographic precip/snow and ridge SWE

assumptions: SSURGO texture in the basin collapses reasonably into ~3 dominant classes (coarse/medium/fine).
NLDAS-2 12 km forcing (CONUS) covers the Naches and gives usable elevation-varying precip across the 1625 m relief.
Per-column QDRAI/QCHARGE is interpreted as vertical potential recharge, not laterally-closed regional recharge.
USGS wells fall within enough of the sampled strata to anchor WTD; validation column count set downstream by well density.
Fan 2013 prior is used both as warm-start IC and as a WTD comparison target; some 1-D-vs-lateral drift is expected.
open_questions: How many USGS wells with reliable WTD exist inside HUC 17030002, and in which elevation/soil strata?
Does the user accept vertical potential recharge as the deliverable, given no lateral-flow coupling and no recharge observations?
Preferred spin-up length vs warm-start-only, given NLDAS ~10x cost per column-year?
Any acceptable indirect recharge benchmark (e.g. gaged baseflow index) for a sanity check?
